description: Every model VaaniDesk knows how to find, verify and install. A human can add a model here without touching Rust: add a models[] entry, give it an id, a licence, an access level, a source, and one entry per file with its byte count and SHA-256. Unknown keys are rejected on load, so a misspelled field is an error rather than a silent default. See manifests/README.md.

models.description: The speech recognition model VaaniDesk runs, and the one it ships with. 65 Indian languages, a FastConformer encoder and a hybrid TDT/RNNT decoder, exported to ONNX by scripts/export_sravaani_onnx.py. Installed: 887 MB, which is the fp16 encoder (845 MiB), the fp32 decoder, the SentencePiece tokenizer, the mel filterbank and window, and the config.

files.note: Production encoder. Native fp16 graph I/O, so the features must be converted with F16Tensor::from_f32. This is the file that has to be streamed, not read: 845 MiB.

TDT emission step, fp32. Must stay fp32: its LSTM state is threaded through every step of a whole utterance. Request logits/h_out/c_out by name; target_length is dead but cannot be removed from the graph.
SentencePiece unigram, 5000 pieces, copied out of the Hugging Face snapshot by the exporter. Without it the engine cannot open at all.
400 x f32, torch.hann_window(400, periodic=False). Symmetric, not periodic. Never pad or shorten it; the zero-padding to n_fft=512 happens in the front end at load time.
Mel filterbank, 32896 x f32 = 128 x 257, row-major.
Front-end parameters. log_zero_guard_value is exactly 2^-24, not NeMo's 1e-5; changing it changes the normalisation of the low-energy bins.
Hyper-parameters, mirrored from the Hugging Face config. SraVaaniConfig::load reads it and validates the invariants the decode loop relies on.

fp32 reference encoder, 1.65 GiB. The app never opens it; it exists so the fp16 graph can be compared against its own reference (99.609% argmax agreement, measured). Optional because its absence costs nothing at runtime, and deliberately not deleted: removing it would remove the only way to re-run that parity check.
Copied from the Hugging Face snapshot by the exporter. Records which snapshot the weights came from.

The exporter's own sha256 log. Known stale for encoder.fp16.onnx (it still records the pre-inline split into .onnx plus .onnx_data), which is exactly why this manifest carries hashes measured from the files that are actually on disk instead of trusting artefacts.json.
